summary: This note describes the executive offices that support prime ministers, noting that they are called the Office of the Prime Minister in Canada and other Commonwealth countries, Cabinet Office in the United Kingdom, and the Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet in Australia. It also covers how constitutions have assigned the power to request a parliamentary dissolution, shifting from cabinet or government as a whole to the prime minister in the UK in 1918 and to the Taoiseach in the 1937 Irish constitution. The note closes with examples of prime minister titles and devolved leader titles in other countries.
one_line: Overview of prime ministers' executive offices, the historical shift in who may request parliamentary dissolution, and national titles for the office.
key_facts: The Prime Minister's executive office is usually called the Office of the Prime Minister in Canada and other Commonwealth countries.
In the United Kingdom, the prime minister's executive office is called the Cabinet Office.
In Australia, the equivalent office is called the Prime Minister's Department or the Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet.
Some Prime Minister's offices include the role of Cabinet.
Older constitutions often vested the power to request a dissolution of parliament in the cabinet.
In the United Kingdom, the tradition whereby the prime minister requests a dissolution of parliament dates back to 1918.
Before 1918, the entire government made the request for a dissolution of parliament in the UK.
The modern 1937 Irish constitution grants the Taoiseach the right to request a dissolution.
The 1922 Irish Free State Constitution vested the dissolution power in the Executive Council, the then name for the Irish cabinet.
Bahrain's prime minister, Sheikh Khalifah bin Sulman Al Khalifah, has been in the post since 1970.
Sheikh Khalifah bin Sulman Al Khalifah is the longest serving non-elected prime minister, according to the note.
In the UK, the leaders of the Scottish, Northern Irish and Welsh Governments are styled First Minister, where devolved government is in place.
In India, the Prime Minister is referred to as "Pradhan Mantri", meaning "prime minister".
In Pakistan, the prime minister is referred to as "Wazir-e-Azam", meaning "Grand Vizier".
